title: Unsupported model output drives sensitive decisions
description: An application may act on fabricated or incorrectly grounded model output when it treats generated statements as verified facts.
mitigation: Require authoritative sources and deterministic validation for consequential decisions; record uncertainty and route unresolved cases to a qualified reviewer.
verification: Compare generated claims with cited authoritative records and test invalid or absent citations before any consequential action.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Human approval can conceal the actual agent action
description: An agent can present a persuasive but incomplete summary while the proposed tool arguments authorize a different target, amount or side effect.
mitigation: Bind approval to immutable action parameters and show the exact target, authorization scope and side effects outside model-generated text.
verification: Alter a proposed tool call after approval; execution must reject the changed parameters.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Autonomous agents can act beyond the assigned objective
description: An agent with persistent execution and broad tools may continue unrequested actions without a deterministic task boundary or independent stop control.
mitigation: Enforce task-scoped capabilities, explicit completion conditions and revocable execution outside the model; record actions and allow immediate cancellation.
verification: Cancel a test task and attempt a new unassigned action; neither the agent nor descendants may keep acting.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Native memory access may exceed allocated bounds
description: Native parsers and unsafe FFI code may read or write outside an allocated buffer when processing attacker-controlled sizes. Architecture presence alone does not establish a memory defect.
mitigation: Prefer memory-safe implementations; review unsafe boundaries, validate lengths before allocation and copying, and enable compiler hardening.
verification: Run sanitizers, fuzzers and boundary-value tests on the relevant parser; require a reproducible source-level failure before confirming a vulnerability.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Native object lifetime errors may permit use after free
description: Unsafe concurrent or callback-driven native code can retain references after an object's lifetime ends. A code or runtime trace is required to establish this weakness.
mitigation: Use ownership-safe data structures and synchronization; minimize unsafe FFI lifetimes and run address/thread sanitizers.
verification: Exercise cancellation, concurrent callbacks and error cleanup paths with sanitizers and confirm ownership remains valid.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Unchecked native failure results may terminate a service
description: Failed parsing or allocation may lead to a null dereference in a native service. This is a review hypothesis until a relevant source path or failure is shown.
mitigation: Check fallible API results, use bounded allocations and propagate errors safely without dereferencing absent objects.
verification: Fault-inject allocation and parse failures in tests; each path must return a bounded error rather than crash.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Mobile deep links may cross authorization boundaries
description: A mobile deep link or exported component may expose a sensitive operation without independently verifying the caller and authenticated user.
mitigation: Allowlist app-link destinations, validate parameters and enforce authorization inside the invoked operation; do not rely on navigation state.
verification: Invoke exported routes from an untrusted test app and while logged out; sensitive actions must be denied.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.

title: Cookie-authenticated state changes require CSRF protection review
description: Where browsers automatically attach authentication cookies, a cross-origin request may trigger a state change unless the application validates request origin or an anti-CSRF token. Cookie authentication must first be established.
mitigation: Enforce anti-CSRF tokens or a rigorously validated origin policy for state changes; use secure cookie attributes as defense in depth.
verification: Test a cross-site state-changing request with an authenticated test browser; verify rejection without the required origin or token.
preconditions: Verify the described technology and operation are present; obtain code, configuration or a controlled test before confirming this hypothesis.
